data.long_meaning: From the Greek name Εἰρήνης (Irene), meaning 'peace'. The name was borne by several saints, including St. Ireneaus of Lyons (AD 130-200), who was a bishop and theologian known for his opposition to Gnosticism. The name Ireneusz carries the meaning “Peace, War” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ireneusz usually hope their child will grow to embody peace, war and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ireneus has a rich cultural history within the Christian faith. It is derived from the Greek word 'Irene', meaning peace. In ancient Greeks, Irene was considered the goddess of peace, harmony, and reconciliation. Through the influence of early Christianity, the name Ireneus became associated with peaceful individuals and the ideologies of Christianity and harmony in personal and spiritual relationships.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Ireneus is rooted in its Greek origins, as 'Irene' symbolizes peace. In the context of Christianity, the name is a reminder of the peace that comes from a deep faith and understanding of God's love. St. Ireneaus, an early Christian theologian, reflected the spiritual depth that is associated with the name. He is known for his unyielding faith despite persecution, and his astute theological explanations that helped to advance early Christian thought.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ireneusz (Erasmus in Greek): A beacon of peace and wisdom, named after Saint Ireneaus of Lyons, known for his advocacy of unity in the early Christian church. His writings continue to inspire harmony and reconciliation.

biblical_reference.note: Not directly mentioned in the Bible, but related to the concept of peace in Christian tradition

historical_references.reference: Ireneus of Lyons was a prominent early Christian theologian and bishop, known as a 'father of the early Church'. He lived in the late 1st and early 2nd centuries AD. He was a student of Polycarp, who was a disciple of the apostle John. Ireneus is believed to have written Against Heresies, an important early Christian text that refutes various Gnostic and other heresies.

Ireneus played a significant role in the development of the doctrine of the Trinity. He wrote extensively on the subject, arguing that there is only one God in three distinct persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This teaching was later formalized at the Council of Nicaea in 325 AD.

modern_usage.modern_context: Ireneusz (Latin: Jerome of Stridon, or simply Jerome) was a prominent theologian and scholar of Late Antiquity. Born in present-day Croatia around 342 AD, he is best known for his translations of the Bible from Greek and Hebrew into Latin, as well as his commentaries on the writings of the Church Fathers. In modern context, his name is commonly associated with Catholicism in Poland, where he is revered as a national saint. Additionally, his works are frequently cited in discussions of Eastern Orthodox theology and in scholarly studies of patristics, especially on LinkedIn, Academia.edu, and Google Scholar platforms.
